answer: A stake-bonded reputation ledger makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit that grows with the work it claims, like a willow bending under weight it cannot fake. A newcomer starts as a relic of zero history and earns trust only through verified, attested tasks, while a sonnet of repeated honest attestations builds its standing over time. An attacker spinning up thousands of clones must fund every deposit and do real work for each one, so the cost of the attack scales linearly while honest agents pay once.
